findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, so the MySQL endpoint receives a public IP and is reachable from the internet. Combined with the hardcoded admin username this exposes the database directly to external attackers.
storage_encrypted = false leaves the database storage, snapshots and read replicas unencrypted, so any access to the underlying volumes exposes all catalog data in plaintext.

The EC2 user_data script embeds the master DB password (var.password) into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc in plaintext; user data is readable from instance metadata and persists on disk, leaking the database master credential.

The launch user_data writes the RDS master username and password into a world-readable web-served include file (/var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc) and installs it on the host, exposing database credentials to anyone with instance access or metadata access.

The instance role grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource '*' — full administrative access to storage, compute and database services. Any compromise of the app server yields complete account takeover of data and infrastructure.

MySQL port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR, allowing any host in the VPC (including the internet-facing app server and any future workloads) to reach the database rather than restricting to the specific application security group.
All outbound traffic (protocol -1, 0.0.0.0/0) is permitted from the database security group, allowing a compromised database to exfiltrate data or establish connections to arbitrary external hosts.
The master username is hardcoded as 'admin', a well-known default that aids credential-guessing and brute-force attacks against the publicly accessible database.

The user_data deploys a PHP application that builds SQL and uses mysql without prepared statements; the interpolated values combined with the exported public DNS output increase the exposure of the web app to injection attacks.
The output 'catalog_app_public_dns' exposes the application server's public DNS name, aiding discovery of a host that serves the DB credential include file.
